key_insight: Intrinsic Fréchet means can be approximated on an unknown manifold using only local samples and an observation metric, without explicit knowledge of its geometry.
engineering_relevance: The method supports averaging structured, non-Euclidean data, such as probability distributions in Wasserstein space.
method: Adaptively sample the unknown compact manifold and construct a graph.
Approximate geodesic interpolation to iteratively minimize the Fréchet objective.
Extend ISOMAP metric-equivalence guarantees to Riemannian ambient spaces.
evidence_signal: Under stated assumptions, the analysis guarantees an O(1/T) expected objective gap using at most Õ(T^(4d+3)) sampled points; numerical experiments demonstrate effectiveness.
watch_item: The sampling bound grows steeply with intrinsic dimension d, raising scalability concerns despite the convergence guarantee.
paper_title: Computing Fréchet on Unknown Submanifolds of Riemannian Manifolds
